title: What to eat
intro: Tottori's two food headlines are wagyu and crab — but the crab most guides mean (matsuba-gani) is a November–March catch and isn't landed during an Oct 20–23 trip. Beni-zuwaigani (red snow crab) runs September–June and is what's actually available, worth asking for by name at a ryokan dinner rather than at a standalone restaurant.

items.name: Yakiniku Masashige
items.how: ≈10–15 min bus or short taxi from Kurayoshi Station.
items.price: ¥2,800–¥6,600 per person (4 Tottori Wagyu course tiers)
items.why: Whole-cow-sourced Tottori Wagyu at a genuinely local price point, with private rooms that scale to a group.
items.crowd_tip: The restaurant's own online booking widget won't take a party of 8 — its selector tops out lower and tells you to call. Book by phone (private rooms run 2–60 across 116 total seats, so 8 is well within real capacity).

items.name: Menya Hachibee
items.hours: ⚠ Lunch ≈10:30–14:00, dinner ≈17:30–20:00 per local coverage — not confirmed against a qualifying primary source
items.closed: ⚠ Reported as Thursdays, unconfirmed against a primary source
items.how: Short taxi or walk from Kurayoshi Station; a counter-and-tables ramen shop, not set up for a party of 8 to book ahead.
items.why: Gyukotsu (beef-bone broth) ramen — a Tottori specialty most visitors never hear of — with a past Michelin Guide selection per local coverage.
items.crowd_tip: Small space — counter, table, and a tatami platform, no private room — and two independent 2025 accounts both describe it getting crowded at lunchtime. For a party of 8: arrive right at opening, or split across two visits/times.
